annotations.text:
The range slider is the one that earns its place: transcribing 2h17m is eight minutes, and most of a service is not worth analysing. Everything else here already exists as a setting — this just asks before the run instead of after.

No credits, no plan banner, no genre picker. Chop Shop has none of those.

The clips become the screen. Today they are a narrow column beside a big source player, which is backwards — the source is context, the clips are the work.

The grid is vertical because the output is vertical.

Opening one clip: player, Claude's reason, the transcript around it, and the four things you can actually do with it. Export to Premiere is real and already built.

No publish-to-social, no upscale — inventing those in a mockup only disappoints later.

The transcript is the edit surface: strike a word and it leaves the render. Everything in the tool rail already exists in the code — cuts, zooms, subject tracking, B-roll, music, LUTs — it has just never had anywhere to live.

Four tracks, not fifty. This edits one clip; the multi-track timeline is a separate workspace and stays that way.
